svg.title: Humanoid robot – Raspberry Pi 3B wiring diagram
svg.desc: Signal wiring for the humanoid robot: Raspberry Pi 3B/3B+ 40-pin header with PCA9685, DHT22, HC-SR04, MCP3008 (MQ-2 and battery dividers), MAX98357A, buzzer driver, LEDs, buttons and camera.

g.text: ▼ USB / Ethernet end of the board
Raspberry Pi 3B / 3B+ · circles = physical pin numbers, labels = BCM GPIO names
Sheet 1 of 2: signal wiring · power: power_diagram.svg · tables: WIRING.md
Header orientation: Pi seen from above with the USB/Ethernet ports pointing DOWN;
odd pins (1…39) are the inner row, even pins (2…40) the board-edge row.
Match the GND / V+ / PWM labels
6.0 V from the servo buck + 1000 µF; the SERVO
2 LEDs per colour, each with its own 330 Ω
powers the Pi through the header
set 5.10 V with a meter first
latches in software; hold MODE 2 s to reset.
The latching SERVO E-STOP switch that cuts servo power
sits before the 6 V buck — see power_diagram.svg.
= common GND (any Pi GND pin / GND bus)
5V RAIL = 5.1 V buck output = Pi pins 2 & 4 (MQ-2, MAX98357A, buzzer).
GND BUS (⏚) = buck / battery − = every Pi GND pin. All grounds are joined.
6V SERVO RAIL = 6.0 V servo buck output (+1000 µF) → PCA9685 V+ only.
Avoid: GPIO20 (pin 38, I²S), GPIO7 (pin 26, SPI CE1), ID_SD/ID_SC (27, 28).
GND pin 30 is free. Dashed label = spare, red ✕ = do not use.
⚠ COMMON GROUND required • NEVER power servos from the Pi • Pi GPIO is 3.3 V ONLY
Set both bucks with a multimeter before connecting (servo 6.0 V, Pi 5.1 V). Power the Pi alone first, then add one part at a time. Full checklist: WIRING.md
